# Robot tennis: program play (match)

You play robot tennis against a scripted opponent (you are seat `A`). Robot singles tennis on a regulation court in real time (slowed down): a Franka Panda arm with a racket on an x-y rail base, the ball with drag, Magnus lift, a hard-court bounce and a racket impact law; first to 5 points; format match: you against a scripted computer opponent (levels 1-4, `game spec` match.opponent_level), format duel: two players; the players serve (ITF Rules 16-22, tie-break order).
This task is generated from `sports/tennis/sport.toml` (task `tennis-match-wallclock-program-standard`).

## Time
The world runs in real time at 1/S of real speed (S = `timing.slowdown` in `game spec`); your thinking costs game time. At the end of every unit the world freezes for the reviews.

Whenever the world freezes for a review (after every unit: a point, a shot, a heat; see `game spec`), send `game ready "WHY" "PLAN"` (a short review) before the next unit starts.
The match is graded when your session ends: stay until it is over. **If your session ends before the match is over, you lose the match** (a valid result, success 0), also if you never sent `game start`.

## Write a program
You may write a program that observes, measures in the images, computes your next action and sends it, without a
new model response for each action. You stay in the loop: watch its log, and stop, fix and restart it whenever
needed. Only you send `game start` and `game ready`.

- Use only the camera images, the service's replies and this document; no simulator internals or hidden state.
- One action at a time: an action sent before the previous one has returned is refused (HTTP 429).
- Your container: Python 3.12 with numpy, SciPy and Pillow; no internet during the match. Keep your scripts, logs
  and notes in `/app/output/`.

## Interface
Use the `game` command, or the same calls as HTTP with JSON at `http://sim:8000/<SEAT>/` (your seat is `$SEAT`):

| `game` command | HTTP | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `game spec` | `GET /spec` | the actions (types, fields, ranges), the cameras with their intrinsics, the rule constants |
| `game status` | `GET /status` | the current state, no image |
| `game start` | `POST /start {}` | you are ready; the match begins when every seat has started |
| `game wait DT` | `POST /wait {"dt": DT}` | let DT game seconds pass (0 < DT <= 1) |
| `game observe` | `POST /observe {}` | the state and the camera images (one PNG of tiles: `observation.tiles`) |
| `game act JSON` | `POST /act JSON` | one action |
| `game none ` | `POST /act {"type":"none", ...}` | one action (`game spec` lists the fields and ranges) |
| `game ready "WHY" "PLAN"` | `POST /ready {"why":"...","plan":"..."}` | your review after each of your actions |

Errors: 400 = an invalid action (nothing happens), 409 = not now (not your turn, or a review is due), 429 = one
action in flight, or more than 20 requests per second or 4 open requests from your seat (empty body: retry more slowly).

## Rules
- robot singles tennis on a regulation court in real time (slowed down): a Franka Panda arm with a racket on an x-y rail base, the ball with drag, Magnus lift, a hard-court bounce and a racket impact law; first to 5 points; format match: you against a scripted computer opponent (levels 1-4, `game spec` match.opponent_level), format duel: two players; the players serve (ITF Rules 16-22, tie-break order).
- `match`: first to 5 points; from 4:4 a player must lead by 2 (no cap: 5:4, 6:5, ... go on until a lead of 2); the match also ends after 400 racket hits or 40 points played: then the player with more points wins, at equal points the player who won the last point
- `serve`: the players serve (ITF Rules 16-22). Order (tie-break, Rule 5 b): the first server serves point 1, then each player serves two points in turn (format match: you serve first; duel: match.first_server); the serving half alternates every point, point 1 from the right half (state.serve.court). The window opens 1.0 s after the point starts and closes 6 s later (state.serve.opens_in_s, deadline_in_s). Your base must be at rest (< 0.1 m/s) behind your base line (y <= -11.885) between the centre mark and the singles sideline of the serving half. {'type':'toss','pos':[X,Y,Z],'height':H}: when it takes effect (the act lead) the ball is at that point (0.3 <= Z <= 2.4, within 1.3 m horizontally of your base) and rises straight up by H (0 <= H <= 1.0; 0: dropped), no spin; then hit it with an act before it lands (the act may be sent before the toss). The serve must first land in the service box diagonally opposite (lines are in). Faults (a second serve from the same half; a second fault, a double fault, loses the point): out of the box, into the net, a foot fault (your base moves more than 0.10 m between the toss and the strike), the toss missed while a stroke is under way (a toss let drop without a stroke is tossed again, within the window), no toss within the window (undue delay). A serve that touches the net and is otherwise good is a let (that serve again, a previous fault stands). The receiver may not hit the serve before it bounces. A point lost on the serve says 'serve_fault:<reason> (double fault: ...)' with reason undue_delay, out_of_box, net, foot_fault, missed_toss or not_completed (each serve's outcome is in the match record); a receiver who hits the serve before it bounces loses the point with 'receive_fault:volley'
- `play`: after the serve has bounced in your service box, or after your opponent's shot (which you may also hit before it bounces), hit the ball once so that it passes over the net, directly or after touching its top edge, and first lands inside your opponent's singles court (lines are in). You lose the point for returning the serve before it bounces, a racket contact beyond the net (y > 0, Rule 24 i), a second bounce on your half, a ball into the net, or a ball that lands out or on your own half; your opponent loses it for the same faults
- `opponent`: format match: a scripted computer opponent that never makes unforced errors and returns every ball it can reach; higher levels react and run faster, reach further and hit faster, wider balls with more spin
- `world`: metres; your own frame: x to your right, y towards the opponent, z up. Court surface z = 0; singles court |x| <= 4.115, |y| <= 11.885; service lines at |y| = 6.40. The net is the plane y = 0, its top 0.914 m at x = 0 rising linearly to 1.07 m at |x| = 5.029. Your half is y < 0
- `robot`: a Franka Panda arm on a 0.55 m pedestal (shoulder 0.88 m above the court) whose base slides on rails over the whole half (|bx| <= 5.9, -15.4 <= by <= -0.4, up to 4 m/s and 8 m/s^2; home (0, -11.4)); the racket head centre is 0.52 m beyond the flange; the strung face is an ellipse of half axes 0.13 m x 0.16 m. Contacts are comfortable 0.6-1.4 m high, about 0.6-0.8 m to the right of and 0.2-0.4 m in front of the base
- `ball`: mass 57.7 g, radius 0.0335 m; gravity 9.81 m/s^2; drag a = -0.0203 |v| v; Magnus lift a = 0.0370 C_L |v|^2 unit(w x v) with C_L = 1/(2 + 1/S), S = 0.0335 |w| / |v|; the spin w is constant in flight
- `court_bounce`: the normal velocity reverses with restitution 0.76; friction (coefficient 0.6) acts on the ball's contact point until it rolls (the tangential impulse is the smaller of 0.6 x the normal impulse and what stops the sliding); the ball's moment of inertia is 0.55 m r^2
- `net`: a ball whose centre comes within its radius of the net's top edge bounces off the edge by the same law (restitution 0.3, friction 0.3) and play goes on; a ball that meets the net lower down stops there
- `racket_contact`: the ball leaves as if the racket head moved 5 times faster than its delivered velocity (V = 5 x the head velocity). In the frame moving with V, with n the unit face normal towards the ball, the normal component reverses with restitution 0.82 (at the head centre, up to 25 % less towards the frame) and friction (coefficient 0.4) acts as in the court bounce. Without the friction: v_out = v_in - 1.82 ((v_in - V).n) n
- `act`: high level: {'type':'act','t':T,'pos':[PX,PY,PZ],'normal':[NX,NY,NZ],'vel':[VX,VY,VZ],'base':[BX,BY] (optional)}: the racket's state at contact, T s after the act takes effect: the head centre, the string-face normal (towards the incoming ball), the head velocity (m/s) and optionally the base position at contact (default: the forehand stance, base = (PX - 0.62, PY - 0.30)). Limits: 0 < T <= 5, |x| <= 6.5, -16 <= y <= 0, 0.1 <= z <= 2.4, speed <= 8 m/s. The act is accepted at the next control step and takes effect `act.lead_steps` steps later (`game spec`; the stroke is planned meanwhile); it replaces the stroke under way. The delivered state scatters by about 5 mm, 0.5 degrees and 2 %. {'type':'move','base':[BX,BY]} sets the base's rest position (where the base goes whenever no stroke is under way; home after each point); {'type':'none'} cancels the stroke (the arm returns to its ready pose); both take effect at the next step; `toss` (serve) takes effect after the act lead. Each player's execution scatter is independent of the opponent's within a match: your acts draw your own seeded stream, and the scripted opponent's choices draw others; format duel: the two matches of a duel pair (the same seed, the first server swapped) swap the scatter sequences, so over the pair both players meet the same draws
- `lowlevel`: low level: {'type':'traj','q':[[base_x, base_y, q1..q7], ...]}: joint targets, one per 10 ms control step from the next step on (then the arm returns to its ready pose), each within the joint ranges and speed limits of `game spec` joints; move, none and toss as above (toss: at the next step)
- `observation`: a PNG of 2 rows x 4 columns of 640 x 480 tiles: row 1 a camera behind and above your base line looking down the court, row 2 a camera at the side of the court (x < 0) looking along +x (your half on the right); the columns are frames 40 ms apart, newest on the right, with each frame's step and game time (view_steps, view_sim_times) and view_leg_ids (a new id each time the ball is served or hit). No ball coordinates: the ball is drawn enlarged, a yellow-green sphere of radius 9 cm centred on its true position. `game spec` gives both cameras' poses and intrinsics (pinhole, 45 degree vertical field of view, focal length 579.4 px, principal point at the tile centre). The state gives your robot (robot_base_xy, q_arm, racket_pos, racket_normal), the bounces you heard (side and time, no position), whether the ball is coming to you, and the serve (you_serve, you_receive_serve, serve: phase waiting / open / tossed / done, court, serve_number, opens_in_s, deadline_in_s, tossed_at_step and the toss point and height, also the opponent's)
- `duel`: format duel: another agent controls an identical robot across the net; in each player's frame its own half is y < 0 and its base's home is (0, -11.4). The players serve by the serve rules above, match.first_server first
- Winner: first to 5 points (from 4:4 by 2, no cap); at the match limit (400 hits or 40 points played) the player with more points; at equal points the player who won the last point; then (last resort, not from the rulebook) the player who received first (format match: the opponent, since you serve first). There are no draws.
- Deviation D1 (rulebook 5-7): one tie-break-style game to 5 points instead of games and sets (Rule 5 b, shorter): from 4:4 a lead of 2 is needed, without a cap (the serving order is the tie-break's; since revision wallclock-8 + duel-6, 2026-10-08: the earlier cap of 7 points favoured one serving order whenever the server's point rate was far from 1/2); the match also ends after 400 racket hits or 40 points played: the player ahead wins, at equal points the winner of the last point
- Deviation D2 (rulebook 16): the robot has one arm and holds the racket (Rule 16: a one-armed player may release the ball with the racket): the release is a `toss` command: the ball appears at a declared point (0.3-2.4 m high, within 1.3 m horizontally of the base) and is projected straight up by a declared height (0-1.0 m), without spin; the rulebook allows a release in any direction
- Deviation D3 (rulebook 24 i): only the strings touch the ball: it passes through the racket frame, the arm and the base
- Deviation D4 (rulebook -): the robot moves on rails over its whole half (|bx| <= 5.9, -15.4 <= by <= -0.4; up to 4 m/s and 8 m/s^2); the stance rules are judged on the base: at the release it must be at rest (< 0.1 m/s) with its centre behind the base line between the centre mark and the singles sideline (Rule 16), and a base that moves more than 0.10 m between the release and the strike is a foot fault (Rule 18); a toss from a wrong stance is refused, not faulted
- Deviation D5 (rulebook -): the last resort of the no-draw rule (equal points at the match limit and no point won) is not from the rulebook: the player who received first wins (format match: the opponent, since you serve first)
- Deviation D6 (rulebook 21): the serve window: it opens 1.0 s after the point starts (the receiver is ready) and closes 6 s later (a second serve or a let: opens at once, 4 s for a second serve); no toss within it is a service fault (undue delay), every time (the rulebook leaves the timing to the officials; no disqualification)
- Deviation D7 (rulebook 5 b): format match: you serve the first point; duel: the first server is match.first_server (the runner plays both orders; there is no toss for service)

## Geometry and physics
Everything you need is in `game spec`: the world frame, the release point, the cameras (pose, field of view, size,
`focal_px`, `principal_point_px`; pinhole: u = cx + f * x_right / depth, v = cy - f * y_up / depth) and the
execution scatter. The physics engine is mujoco (robots, PD-controlled joints at 1 ms) + a point-mass ball integrated at 1 ms (sim/tn.py).
